rv.q: In truth, I didn't find a great deal of it especially amusing, (perhaps the detail is still too raw?) but the light groaning and nods of recognition from the largely middle-aged white males ranged about the audience, was encouraging.
This easily entertaining show humorously charts Truss’s lifetime of egotism and vacuousness, although it lacks the extra bite that would make it truly satirical gold.
Sadly, a reliance on quick-fix easy laughs removes any possibility of that.
Alas, it was dull, humourless, and felt like a chore.

cn.t: Emma Wilkinson Wright delivers an assured performance in this frantic farce about Britain's shortest-serving PM, but critics find it relies too heavily on cheap laughs and lacks the satirical bite to match its ripe subject matter.
